page: Amazon Web Services r6id.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The virtual machine provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 54 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, SHA extensions, and cryptographic acceleration through AES and VAES.

The instance is provisioned with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive workloads. For local temporary storage, r6id.xlarge includes a bundled 237 GB NVMe SSD. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs configured on this instance type. Network connectivity provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

In synthetic benchmarks, the r6id.xlarge exhibits solid single-thread performance, ranking in the middle tier with a Geekbench single-core score of 1582.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1889.59. It also achieves mid-tier marks for cryptographic operations and small-model language inference text generation (93.21 tokens per second). However, due to its modest total core count of 2 physical cores (4 vCPUs), aggregate parallel metrics register in lower percentiles. The PassMark CPU score reaches 5786.32, and multi-core Geekbench performance scores at 3392.0.

Memory subsystem benchmarks show uncached large-block read speeds of 29.29 GB/s and write speeds of 24.41 GB/s. Redis SET operations measured at 3.97 million operations per second, while static web throughput reached 6.53 GB/s. With high memory density per core paired with fast direct-attached NVMe storage, the r6id.xlarge is aligned for in-memory caching systems, distributed datastore nodes, batch processing, and mid-sized transactional databases requiring high RAM ratios without requiring high parallel core counts.

Configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, it includes 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Storage consists of a bundled 237 GB NVMe SSD, alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile and no GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-range single-core throughput, including a 1582.0 Geekbench single-core score and steady single-threaded decompression metrics, balanced against modest multi-core capacity reflecting its 4 vCPU allocation. Memory tests show 29.29 GB/s uncached reads and 24.41 GB/s writes. The combination of dense memory allocation and local NVMe storage positions the r6id.xlarge for mid-scale in-memory databases, key-value stores, and memory-bound transactional caching workloads.
